title: Big Is Bad
coreMove: Question the reflex that shrinks goals for comfort, then test whether a larger aim is legitimate and actionable.
sourcePressure: This lie chapter challenges suspicion toward large aims while keeping scale tied to legitimacy rather than fantasy or dream-big rhetoric.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Pumping the reader up to dream big without standards or limits.

hook: A single choice changes the whole day
The real priority is hiding under the busy work
Big Is Bad as a generic focus opener
counterintuition: Focus is harder than it looks
tryThisNow: Set a timer and list priorities
Write down your one thing without a concrete context
examples: generic office worker choosing email or strategy

exampleSpecs.stakes: three rural counties have no pediatric appointments
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she stops calling the second van unrealistic and checks whether staffing, route density, and school demand make the larger goal responsible
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a county map with three school nurse pins and one blank van route

exampleSpecs.stakes: players age out because only one city has games
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he refuses the safe single-tournament plan and drafts a three-city pilot with equipment sharing constraints visible
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three gym reservation forms lined beside a stack of wheel rims

exampleSpecs.domain: sea wall redesign after repeated flooding
exampleSpecs.stakes: the town wants a patch that will fail in five years
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she asks the council to compare the larger redesign to repeated emergency repairs instead of labeling it too big
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a flood line drawn across a brick wall in the council chamber lobby

exampleSpecs.stakes: students wait months for advanced math materials
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she tests whether a statewide production hub is bold enough to solve the delay rather than merely improving one school's queue
exampleSpecs.firstImage: raised braille pages stacked beside a half-empty shipping shelf

exampleSpecs.domain: independent clinic adopting same-day addiction treatment
exampleSpecs.stakes: people are lost between referral and appointment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he predicts same-day intake is too big, then maps the missed handoffs and sees the larger move is the only one that removes them
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a referral sheet with three missed-call marks beside an empty exam room

exampleSpecs.domain: regional maker fair moving from hobby booths to apprenticeship pipeline
exampleSpecs.stakes: local manufacturers cannot fill trainee roles
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the organizer sees booth attendance was not the big enough measure and builds a pilot matching students to shop mentors
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a soldering station beside a manufacturer's unsigned apprenticeship form

tryThisNowSpec: Take one goal you have quietly downsized and write what evidence would make the larger version responsible rather than reckless.
